EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East situation remains highly volatile, dominated by significant escalations in direct US-Iran military exchanges and ongoing intense negotiations for a Phase 2 ceasefire in Gaza. US forces conducted widespread airstrikes across Iran in retaliation for Iranian missile attacks, while Iran claimed to have destroyed US F-35 fighter jets in Jordan and attacked Kuwaiti territory. Meanwhile, progress is reported on a Gaza ceasefire roadmap that includes Hamas disarmament under international supervision, though Israel continues targeted killings of Hamas commanders.

IRAN
The United States launched a heavy wave of airstrikes against dozens of targets across Iran, including military command centers, missile and drone facilities, coastal defense positions, and naval capabilities. Targets were reported in Khuzestan (Ahvaz, Abadan, Shushtar), Hormozgan (Qeshm Island, Bandar Abbas, Kish Island), and Fars Province (Kazerun, Noorabad, Farashband). Iranian sources reported explosions in these areas, with claims of damage to two student dormitories in Ahvaz, an empty sports hall in Farashband, a military base near Kazerun, and Information Ministry/IRGC Intelligence headquarters in Ahvaz’s Golestan neighborhood, leading to power outages. US HIMARS missiles were reportedly launched from Kuwait against targets in Iran.

In retaliation, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed strikes on the US Ali Al-Salem airbase in Kuwait, destroying two drone hangars and a fuel depot, and on the Al-Azraq airbase in Jordan, claiming the complete destruction of three F-35 fighter jets and severe damage to three others, along with technical personnel casualties. Jordan confirmed intercepting five Iranian missiles without reporting F-35 destruction. Kuwait reported an Iranian attack on a Chinese company building in its northern region, killing one worker and causing significant damage.

Casualties from the US strikes in Iran include a father, mother (Qaisar and Zahra Jafari), and their two-year-old child (Sinai) killed in a residential building on Qeshm Island, with two other children injured. Twenty families were evacuated in Qeshm. Three IRGC personnel from Zanjan province (Mahmoud Malajabari, Mohammadreza Cheraghi, Jamal Amiri) were reportedly killed in US attacks.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a flashpoint; the IRGC stated it is their territory, will not tolerate interference, and will remain closed as long as US threats persist, following an alleged drone attack on two oil tankers, one of which caught fire. Oil prices have risen to $93/barrel. The US Treasury sanctioned eight tankers and ten entities linked to Iran. Iran is reportedly considering importing 400 shoulder-fired air defense missile launchers from China.

ISRAEL
The IDF Chief of Staff, Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir, visited southern Lebanon, asserting readiness for continued war across all fronts and promising to deepen operations and maintain control of captured territories until long-term security is assured. He also emphasized the need for the IDF to grow and strengthen its ground combat forces, noting an increase in Haredi recruitment. In Gaza, IDF strikes killed Ahmad Hisham Mahmoud Louh, a Hamas sniper commander, and Mahmoud Ali Mahmoud Taroush, a Hamas platoon commander involved in the October 7 attack.

Domestically, a significant disciplinary incident occurred at Sde Teiman base where dozens of Givati brigade soldiers abandoned their weapons and base after their commander removed "abnormal event" signs related to "youth traditions." The IDF condemned the incident as a serious disruption and a criminal offense. An Israeli ambulance driver, Amir Hisham Mohammad Titi, was arrested on suspicion of spying for Iran, allegedly collecting intelligence on hospitals, VIPs (including President Herzog and former Defense Minister Gallant's residence), and protest locations. Two Israeli settlement activists illegally crossed into Syria from Mount Hermon and were returned by the IDF.

Politically, Prime Minister Netanyahu met with US President Trump, discussing three options for Iran (a deal, continued naval blockade, or escalated military action) and expressed skepticism about a diplomatic agreement. Netanyahu reportedly proposed phasing out US military aid to Israel over 10 years, seeking a new MOU including $16 billion in direct aid plus substantial support for missile defense and R&D. National Security Minister Ben Gvir opposed any Gaza ceasefire deal that would halt terrorist assassinations. A Channel 13 poll showed Gadi Eisenkot and Netanyahu tied at 23 mandates.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Progress is reported in negotiations for Phase 2 of a Gaza ceasefire agreement. Palestinian sources and the "Peace Council" indicate a "roadmap" involving the disarmament of all Palestinian factions' weapons (light and heavy, tunnels, stockpiles, production sites) under multinational supervision. The agreement would link a complete IDF withdrawal from Gaza to full demilitarization, and Hamas would commit to halting all military activity, recruitment, and rearmament. A key point is that Hamas would have no role in Gaza's future government, openly or behind the scenes, with full authority transferred to a Palestinian committee.

Despite these negotiations, Israeli military operations continue, including the targeted killings of Hamas sniper commander Ahmad Hisham Mahmoud Louh and platoon commander Mahmoud Ali Mahmoud Taroush. An Israeli drone strike was reported in Jabalia, northern Gaza, killing one and injuring several, and another in Yarmouk, central Gaza City. Separately, three Palestinians, including two children, were killed in recent Israeli strikes across the Gaza Strip.

LEBANON
IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir visited southern Lebanon, stating the military is prepared for any scenario and will "push deeper and reach additional areas" if required. He affirmed that the IDF would not retreat from territories captured from Hezbollah until long-term security is secured for northern Israeli communities. Reserve Brigade 55 located dozens of Hezbollah weapons, including Kalashnikovs, grenades, anti-tank missiles, and mortar shells, hidden within civilian infrastructure in Majdal Zoun. Reports also indicated a drone attack in Nabatiyeh, southern Lebanon, and Israeli warplanes entering Beirut airspace.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The United States and Saudi Arabia conducted joint airstrikes against pro-Iranian militias in Iraq. US sources reported approximately 20 Iranian advisors, including Quds Force members, were killed in these strikes, which targeted sites specifically chosen to affect Iranian advisors and disrupt missile and drone capabilities. AP reported six Iranian military advisors killed. Khalid Al-Ayshi, a senior Houthi commander, was also reportedly killed in these strikes. Iraq's top political coalition condemned the US-Saudi strikes as endangering stability, and the Iraqi Islamic Resistance gave the government until August 6 to respond to the aggression, warning that Saudi Arabia could be targeted. Iraq's security forces denied any evidence of attacks on Saudi Arabia originating from Iraqi soil and affirmed that only official forces are responsible for national security. Two Israeli settlement activists illegally crossed into Syria from the Mount Hermon area before being returned by the IDF.

GULF STATES
Kuwait reported an Iranian attack on a Chinese company building in its northern region, resulting in one fatality and significant damage. The IRGC claimed this was part of its retaliation for US actions, specifically targeting the US Ali Al-Salem airbase in Kuwait. US forces reportedly launched HIMARS missiles from Kuwait against targets in Iran. Saudi Arabia's Defense Minister, Prince Khalid bin Salman, informed US Vice President Vance that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman seeks to de-escalate with Iran. Riyadh's King Khaled International Airport experienced a runway closure for maintenance, affecting air traffic. Bahrain's Isa Air Base saw US plane landings. Iran continues talks with Oman regarding the management of the Strait of Hormuz. The Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC) reported a drone attack on two oil tankers (one flagged Marshal Islands, one Isle of Man) in the Black Sea, causing considerable economic damage.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US Launches Widespread Strikes in Iran:** The US Central Command (CENTCOM) conducted "heavy waves of strikes" against dozens of Iranian military and strategic targets across multiple provinces, including Khuzestan, Hormozgan, and Fars.
2.  **Iran Claims Retaliation and Damage to US Assets:** The IRGC claimed retaliatory strikes on the US Ali Al-Salem airbase in Kuwait and the Al-Azraq airbase in Jordan, asserting the destruction of three US F-35 fighter jets and two drone hangars.
3.  **Jordan Intercepts Iranian Missiles:** Jordan confirmed intercepting five Iranian missiles targeting its territory, refuting IRGC claims of F-35 destruction at Al-Azraq.
4.  **Kuwaiti Civilian Fatality in Iranian Attack:** Kuwait reported an Iranian attack on a Chinese company building in northern Kuwait, resulting in one worker killed and significant damage.
5.  **Gaza Ceasefire Progress Reported:** Negotiators reported significant progress on a Phase 2 ceasefire roadmap for Gaza, detailing Hamas disarmament of weapons, tunnels, and production sites under multinational supervision, and linking IDF withdrawal to full demilitarization.
6.  **US-Saudi Strikes Kill Iranian Advisors in Iraq:** Joint US-Saudi airstrikes targeted pro-Iranian militias in Iraq, reportedly killing approximately 20 Iranian advisors, including Quds Force members, drawing strong condemnation and threats of retaliation from Iraqi resistance.
7.  **Israeli Ambulance Driver Arrested for Espionage:** An Israeli ambulance driver was arrested by the Shin Bet on suspicion of spying for Iran, accused of collecting sensitive information on hospitals and VIP movements.
8.  **Strait of Hormuz Tensions:** The IRGC threatened to close the Strait of Hormuz if US interference continues, following an alleged drone attack on two oil tankers in the Black Sea and previous claims of targeting and seizing vessels.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation in the Middle East is critically high, with direct military confrontation between the US and Iran intensifying. Active flashpoints include US airstrikes deep within Iranian territory, reciprocal Iranian missile attacks on US regional bases, and the volatile Strait of Hormuz where Iran threatens closure. The US is considering a broader "punishing air campaign," while Iran's IRGC has issued strong threats of retaliation against any "aggressor." In Iraq, US-Saudi strikes against Iranian proxies and advisors have created a direct confrontation that Iraqi resistance groups have vowed to avenge, raising the specter of expanded regional proxy conflict. While Gaza ceasefire talks offer a glimmer of hope, ongoing IDF targeted killings of Hamas commanders could undermine negotiations. Israel's asserted resolve to deepen operations in Lebanon further compounds regional instability. The potential for miscalculation and rapid escalation across multiple fronts remains significant.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** under President Trump has resumed "very hard" retaliatory strikes against Iran, with CENTCOM confirming attacks on dozens of military and strategic targets. Admiral Brad Cooper, CENTCOM Commander, reportedly prepared plans for a 10-14 day "punishing air campaign." The US Treasury sanctioned Iranian-linked tankers and entities. **Saudi Arabia**, while participating in joint strikes against Iraqi militias, expressed a desire to curb escalation with Iran, contrasting with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's hardline stance. **Kuwait** reported an Iranian attack on a Chinese company building, resulting in a fatality. **Iraq's** political leadership condemned the US-Saudi strikes and initiated a plan to prevent its territory from being used to threaten neighbors, while Iraqi resistance vowed retaliation. **Jordan** confirmed intercepting five Iranian missiles. The **European Union** showed concern over regional stability, with Bulgaria emphasizing diplomacy and de-escalation in a call with Iran, while Iran condemned Bulgaria for allegedly supporting US attacks. A diplomatic spat emerged between the US and **France** over critical UN statements and French military assistance to US bases in Jordan. **China** denied reports of supplying Iran with shoulder-fired missile launchers, asserting a constructive role in de-escalation. **Pakistan** offered to mediate between the US and Iran. **Yemen's** Ansarullah leader condemned the US-Saudi aggression in Iraq and denied attacking Egypt.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions persist in reporting, particularly concerning the claimed effectiveness of Iranian strikes. The IRGC's assertion of destroying three F-35s at Jordan's Al-Azraq base is highly improbable and uncorroborated by Jordanian reports, which merely noted the interception of five missiles. This appears to be a major propaganda effort by the IRGC to project military success and deter further US aggression. Similarly, the IRGC's claim of "targeting and seizing" three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz lacks independent verification. Details surrounding the alleged drone attack on the LNG tanker in Egypt are also ambiguous, with Egyptian authorities initially describing it as a fire. Casualty figures for Iranian advisors in Iraq from US-Saudi strikes vary, ranging from six (AP) to approximately 20 (US officials). There is a reporting gap regarding the specific nature of the "abnormal event" signs removed at Sde Teiman, which triggered the Givati mutiny, as well as the complete extent of damage from US strikes within Iran due to limited independent access. The claim of a B1 bomber from the UK moving to the Middle East by one source is unverified.
